title: Too Good to Eat: Meet the Artist Who Knits Food
paragraphs: Kate Jenkins can make all sorts of dishes, from pasta to pizza to desserts.
There's just one thing — her dishes can't be eaten!

Jenkins is an artist from the UK who is known for her knitted, crocheted and embroidered creations. When she was a child, her grandmother taught her how to knit, and she has been creating things out of yarn ever since.
In the 1990s, she worked as a knitwear designer for big fashion houses, including Ralph Lauren and Marc Jacobs, and she later started her own fashion company.

When Jenkins needed a way to promote her company, she started knitting food, both for fun and to try to get people's attention. That became her first food-themed exhibition, called "Comfort Food," in 2007.
Her food creations were so popular that they became a very important part of her career. Since then, she's created collections based on bakeries, cafes, ice cream shops and more.
Her newest exhibition is called "Kate's Knitalian," which is made to look like an Italian restaurant. It opened on October 30 at the Air Contemporary Gallery in London.

The exhibition has over 100 pieces made by Jenkins, including knitted plates of ravioli, bottles of wine and even a creamy tiramisu. Jenkins wrote on her website that everything was made to look "deliciously real."
All pieces are available to buy, and the exhibition will be open until December 5.

Jenkins also likes to add a little humor to her work. The "restaurant" has a sign saying that it's been rated by the "Stitchelin Guide" — instead of the Michelin Guide — and another that says it's on "Knitadvisor," instead of Tripadvisor!
"Above all, I want my work to make people smile," Jenkins said on her website.
